classification.difficultyReason: Construct a 60° angle by applying the taught equilateral-triangle construction with equal-radius compass arcs.

content.prompt: Use the equilateral triangle construction to construct an angle of $60^\circ$ at the endpoint $A$ of an interval $AB$.

answer.short: An angle of $60^\circ$ at $A$, constructed using equal-radius arcs centred at $A$ and $B$.
answer.worked:
Draw an interval $AB$. With centre $A$ and radius $AB$, draw an arc. Keeping the same compass radius, draw an arc centred at $B$ to intersect the first arc at $C$. Draw the ray $AC$, retaining both construction arcs.

Since $AB=AC=BC$, triangle $ABC$ is equilateral. Therefore $\angle CAB=60^\circ$.

spec.description: Authored completed construction. Equal-radius dashed arcs meet at C; the ray AC forms 60° with AB. Dotted BC shows the equilateral-triangle justification.
